description: NSW Ancillary Mining Areas is a dataset listed in NSW Government open data portal (data.nsw.gov.au), Australia, an open data portal, published or maintained by Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD). Ancillary Mining Areas (AMAs) are designated land zones used for infrastructure that supports mining operations (such as roads, dams, stockpiles, buildings, and water‑management systems) without being part of the extraction site. They require specific approvals under mining legislation to ensure environmental compliance, rehabilitation, and appropriate land‑use management. Coverage: New South Wales. The portal files it under the publisher Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD). Its tags are GEOSCIENCES-Geology, INDUSTRY-Mining, Mining. It offers 4 resource(s) in pdf, spatial viewer, wfs, wms. The portal shows 2026-01-26 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is Internal use only. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. Suitability for infrastructure simulation has not been checked. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ditrdcsa-data-nsw.
